## Decisions

- **Model an estimate as one all-or-none object (Estimate | null) rather than three nullable numbers**: M13's columns are est_optimistic/est_likely/est_pessimistic with a num_nonnulls(...) in (0, 3) check, so a half-set estimate is forbidden in the DB; one value makes that state unrepresentable in the app, and the first draft (three required numbers) could not represent an unestimated task at all without faking values. (alternatives: three `number | null` fields (mirrors the columns but allows the illegal half-set); make a/m/b required and exclude unestimated tasks from the list entirely)
- **toPertTasks drops estimate-less tasks instead of letting the engine reject them**: A real board is full of tasks nobody has estimated yet, and the design says such tasks are 'simply left out ("unscheduled" list), not an error'. The filter therefore lives at the engine seam, while a LINK pointing at an unestimated task stays the typed missing-estimate error the engine already returns. (alternatives: pass everything and treat the engine's missing-estimate error as routine; require every caller to pre-filter (easy to get wrong in two places))
- **Criticality in both views comes from schedule.criticalPath membership; the node's own `critical` flag is exposed separately as NetworkRow.critical / onCriticalPath**: PSI-119 established that on a duration tie the reported path is the one carrying the larger variance, so a zero-slack task can be `critical: true` while sitting off the reported path. Exposing both, named, stops a UI from equating them. (alternatives: only the boolean (would mis-highlight bars); only path membership (loses the per-task zero-slack signal))
- **Rows carry days; durationInUnit (÷7) and varianceInUnit (÷49) do the display conversion**: Brief D7 stores calendar days and treats weeks as a display concern. Keeping variance's 7² scaling in one named helper guards the mistake from PSI-119's first draft, where variance was divided by 7. (alternatives: convert inside the row builders (loses the canonical days, and the unit is a render-time choice))
- **Date maths via an explicit +07:00 offset and millisecond arithmetic, never local-time parsing**: boards.project_start is a WIB calendar date and Indonesia has no DST, so a fixed offset is exact; building the instant from '+07:00' and adding ms keeps output identical whatever the browser's timezone is. Verified under TZ=UTC and TZ=America/New_York. (alternatives: new Date(`${date}T00:00:00`) (local time — silently shifts the whole Gantt by the viewer's offset); round ES to whole days (loses the engine's fractional positions))
- **link-guard is a client-side convenience only; the DB stays the authority**: The design says the editor checks cycles client-side 'too ... The DB rejects cycles regardless'. Two concurrent inserts can both pass a client check, so this walk exists for a good error message and a sane combobox, not for integrity. (alternatives: treat the client check as the guard (unsafe under concurrency))
- **Do not install frappe-gantt yet**: C-10/D6 authorise the dependency, but the brief's trap says to check its current API and pin the version at implementation time, and a DOM-only wrapper with no data path cannot be verified by hand this session. (alternatives: install and write the wrapper now against fixture rows (unverifiable until M13 lands))
